title: WhatsApp
summary: 1:1 and group messaging for billions: persistent connections to chat servers, a per-user inbox for offline delivery, sent/delivered/read receipts, end-to-end encryption, and group fan-out.

head: Type
Requirement
rows: 1:1 and group chats (up to ~1k members); text and media
Offline delivery; sent ✓, delivered ✓✓, read (blue) receipts; last seen
End-to-end encryption — servers can't read messages
Delivery to online recipients < 500 ms; messages never lost; per-chat order

blocks.title: Key insight
blocks.text: Unlike Slack, WhatsApp stores messages on the server only until they're delivered. History lives on devices (and user backups).

items.title: Send
items.text: A sends message (client-generated id) to its chat server; server persists to B's inbox and acks → single tick.

items.title: Route
items.text: Look up B's chat server in the session registry; forward if online, else send a push notification.

items.title: Deliver
items.text: B's device receives and acks → server deletes from inbox and sends a delivered receipt to A (double tick).

items.title: Read
items.text: When B opens the chat, B sends a read receipt — just another tiny message routed to A.

items: Ordering per chat: sequence numbers assigned per conversation (or by the sender per chat) and reordered on device.
Dedup with the client message id — retries are safe.

sections.title: Deep dive: end-to-end encryption and groups

items: Signal protocol: each device publishes identity and one-time prekeys; senders establish a session (X3DH) and ratchet keys per message (Double Ratchet).
Server only routes ciphertext; it can't read content.
Groups use **sender keys**: each member distributes a sender key to others once (pairwise-encrypted), then each message is encrypted once and fanned out by the server.
Multi-device: each device has its own keys; the sender encrypts for every device of every recipient.

blocks.title: Say it in the interview
blocks.text: The server is a store-and-forward router for ciphertext. Delivery state is server-side; message history is device-side.

items: Shard inboxes by recipient user id; session registry is a sharded in-memory map with TTL heartbeats.
Media: client encrypts and uploads to blob storage; message carries the URL + key.
Chat server crash: clients reconnect to another server; undelivered messages are still in the inbox.
Large groups: fan-out on the server per member's inbox; cap group size.

cols.title: Device-side history (WhatsApp)
cons: History sync to new devices is hard; backups needed

cols.title: Server-side history (Slack)
cons: Server can read data (no E2E), big storage

items.title: Deep dives
items.text: Receipts flow; ordering/dedup; E2E + sender keys.

items.a: Chat servers update a presence store on connect/disconnect/heartbeat; contacts fetch it on demand rather than subscribing.

items.q: How do you deliver to a phone that's been off for a week?
items.a: The inbox keeps messages (with a retention limit, e.g. 30 days); on reconnect the device drains it.
Lightweight processes per connection and robust supervision made millions of connections per box practical.

items: Per-user inbox until delivered; push if offline.
✓ = server ack, ✓✓ = device ack, blue = read receipt.
Client message ids for dedup; per-chat sequence for order.
Signal protocol; sender keys for groups.
